title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 316: The Laughter Circuit: Roots of Social Mirth
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 316 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Laughter Circuit: Evolutionary Roots of Social Mirth

Paragraph 1. Everybody laughs, even though laughing looks and sounds quite strange. Speaking takes careful thinking, but real laughter happens suddenly without planning. In every country, babies start giggling at four months old, long before they learn to say words. Long ago, famous thinkers like Plato thought laughter was mean and showed people feeling superior to others. However, scientist Dr. Robin Dunbar proves that laughter is actually an ancient natural tool for bringing groups together.

Paragraph 2. Dr. Dunbar studied great apes, such as chimpanzees and orangutans. When young apes play and tickle each other, they make soft panting sounds. Those sounds tell partners that wrestling is friendly fun, not a real fight. Long ago, apes stayed friends by cleaning each other's fur by hand. When early human groups grew bigger than fifty members, cleaning fur took too much time. So laughter grew as a quick way to share friendliness with many friends at once.

Paragraph 3. Laughing also changes chemicals inside the human brain. A good laugh releases natural body chemicals that reduce pain and make people feel calm and trusting. When friends laugh together, their brains share a warm feeling of safety.

Paragraph 4. Still, Dr. Dunbar warns that humour has a darker side too. Friends sometimes tell inside jokes to push strangers outside their group. Also, workers often laugh much more at the jokes of important leaders than bosses laugh at workers' jokes, using polite laughter to stay safe at work.

q5.text: How is real laughter different from speaking?
options: A. Laughter only happens after people learn grammar.
B. Laughter is much quieter than everyday speech.
C. Laughter happens naturally without careful planning.

steps: Đoạn 1: "Speaking takes careful thinking, but real laughter happens suddenly without planning."

q6.text: Why do young apes make panting sounds when wrestling?
options: A. To show the game is friendly and not a real fight
B. To call adult animals to bring them food
C. To scare strangers away from the forest

steps: Đoạn 2: Tín hiệu báo đây là chơi đùa thân thiện chứ không phải đánh nhau thật.

q7.text: Why did early humans stop relying only on cleaning fur to make friends?
options: A. They lost all the hair on their arms and legs.
B. Groups grew too large to clean everyone by hand.
C. Cleaning fur caused painful skin illnesses.

steps: Đoạn 2: Nhóm đông quá 50 cá thể nên chải lông thủ công tốn quá nhiều thời gian.

q8.text: According to Paragraph 4, how do workers sometimes use laughter?
options: A. As a polite way to stay safe with bosses
B. As a method to solve hard math problems
C. As a way to make strangers feel welcome

steps: Đoạn 4: Cười lịch sự với cấp trên để giữ an toàn nơi làm việc.
